main_text.p: naturæ leges tum procreatrices tum conserua-trices indixit. Itaq; animantium, stirpium, lapidum & metallorum omnium quæcunq; fuerunt & esse possunt, formas, vnius cœli formæ potestate comprehendit, quæ innumerabilibus quasi grauidata formis omnia gignit & ex se fundit, & sic vna vis & facultas præ se fert omniumSpecies rerum à cœlo. Caducorum vires, vt ita cœlum nullo semine multas proferat tum animantes tum stirpes, at semen sine cœlo non generet quicquam, sed gignendis rebus materiam duntaxat & conuenienter apparet ac instruat, cœ-lum vero in apparatam illam materiam spe-ciem summamq; perfectionem immittat, vitamque suscitet in omnibus, lucido spiritu intercedente: hic enim mundi & cœlorum exi-stit vector, in totam vniuersitatem diffusus, rebus singulis simul & specie, & natiuum vitalemq; calorem impertit gignendis illis accommodatū. Is est, q; omnia continet, calore vitaq; fouet, huius vi & ope & inanima quæque per-sistunt, & animata sui quæq; generis habent animam, alia nutrientem quidem, alia sentientem, alia rationis participem. Sic tamen vis illa cœlitus demissa rebus sese accommodat, sic singulis inseruit, vt quantum cuiusque natura desiderat, quantū ipsa subiecti[?] ratio & conditio ferre potest, tantundē exhibeat. page.notes: Marginal notes, left: "Species rerum à cœlo." beside the line "omnium Caducorum vires", and "Spiritus formarum dator." beside "lum vero in apparatam" (transcribed as a note at the place of "cœ-lum"; the second note is in the left margin and was not separately placed in the text). The catchword "per &" is the last line at the right. The right side of the scan shows show-through from the facing page and is omitted. The word "subiecti" is doubtful: the scan reads roughly "snbicti" with a damaged letter.
